title: Post in Prairie Bend County Neighbors: "PIPELINE EXPLODED"

fields.avatarBrief: man in his fifties in a camo cap and sunglasses holding up a large flathead catfish on a muddy riverbank, sunny outdoor phone photo
fields.text: PIPELINE EXPLODED at Mill Ridge!! 10,000 barrels in the Kaw, my buddy at the county says the water is POISONED. Sterling Bluff and the rural water district are pumping it straight into our taps right now. Ironbark hasn't said a WORD. #KawSpill #IronbarkLies
fields.attachedImageBrief: still from a shaky vertical 20-second phone video, play icon over it: black glossy liquid flowing down a grassy roadside drainage ditch in early morning light, a gravel road shoulder and a pickup tailgate at the edge of the frame, river trees in the background

comments.author: Brenda K.
comments.text: My mom is in the nursing home in Sterling Bluff. Do we stop drinking the water?? Has ANYONE official said anything???

comments.author: Prairie 6 News News
comments.text: We're working to confirm details on reports of oil in the Kansas River near Mill Ridge. If you saw it yourself, please send photos or video to our newsroom by message.

comments.author: Gary W.
comments.text: There was no explosion, I live two miles from Mill Ridge and didn't hear a thing. But something stinks out here this morning, that's for sure.

instructorNote: Misinformation inject. When you hand this over, also tell the PIO that Prairie 6 News's assignment desk has emailed: "Confirm 10,000 barrels? Live shot at 7:00." The 10,000-barrel claim is bigger than the plan's 8,400-barrel worst case, so watch that the PIO does not confirm it or argue about it. The PIO should draft a holding statement for clearance that gives only the cleared 2,700–3,500 barrel range and says the cause is unknown. The PIO should also refer drinking-water questions to the utilities and the state, ask for the JIC to stand up, and give the reporter a time for the next update.
